passages.text: Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath son of Levi, along with some Reubenites—Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth—conducted a rebellion against Moses, along with 250 men of Israel renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.
passages.sermon:
Korah was the son of Izhar.
Izhar was the son of Kohath.
Kohath was the son of Levi.
Korah joined with Dathan and Abiram.
Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab.
On, the son of Peleth, also joined them.
On was a descendant of Reuben.
These men gathered together.
They stood before Moses.
Two hundred fifty men of Israel joined them.
These men were leaders of the congregation.
They were chosen representatives in the assembly.
They were well-known men.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח קֹ֔רַח בֶּן־ יִצְהָ֥ר בֶּן־ קְהָ֖ת בֶּן־ לֵוִ֑י וְדָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם בְּנֵ֧י אֱלִיאָ֛ב וְא֥וֹן בֶּן־ פֶּ֖לֶת בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵֽן׃ וַיָּקֻ֙מוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים מִבְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם נְשִׂיאֵ֥י עֵדָ֛ה קְרִאֵ֥י מוֹעֵ֖ד אַנְשֵׁי־ שֵֽׁם׃

passages.text: They came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, “You have taken too much upon yourselves! For everyone in the entire congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
Korah and his followers gathered against Moses and Aaron.
They spoke to Moses and Aaron.
They said, “You have taken too much upon yourselves.
Every person in the congregation is holy.
The LORD is among all the people.
Why do you set yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
passages.original: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶם֮ רַב־ לָכֶם֒ כִּ֤י כָל־ הָֽעֵדָה֙ כֻּלָּ֣ם קְדֹשִׁ֔ים וּבְתוֹכָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וּמַדּ֥וּעַ תִּֽתְנַשְּׂא֖וּ עַל־ קְהַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.
passages.sermon: Moses was the leader of Israel.\r\nMoses heard the words of Korah and his followers.\r\nMoses fell facedown on the ground.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיִּפֹּ֖ל עַל־ פָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then he said to Korah and all his followers, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will reveal who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses, He will bring near to Himself.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Korah and all his followers.
He said, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will show who belongs to Him.
The LORD will show who is holy.
The LORD will bring that person close to Himself.
The LORD will choose someone.
The LORD will bring that chosen person near to Himself.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־ קֹ֜רַח וְאֶֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדָתוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בֹּ֠קֶר וְיֹדַ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֛וֹ וְאֶת־ הַקָּד֖וֹשׁ וְהִקְרִ֣יב אֵלָ֑יו וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַר־ בּ֖וֹ יַקְרִ֥יב אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: You, Korah, and all your followers are to do as follows: Take censers, and tomorrow you are to place fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD. Then the man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you sons of Levi who have taken too much upon yourselves!”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Korah and all his followers.
Moses gave them instructions.
He said, “Korah, take censers for yourself and for all your followers.
Tomorrow, put fire in the censers.
Place incense on the fire.
Do this before the LORD.
The LORD will choose one man.
The man the LORD chooses will be holy.
You sons of Levi have gone too far.”
passages.original: זֹ֖את עֲשׂ֑וּ קְחוּ־ לָכֶ֣ם מַחְתּ֔וֹת קֹ֖רַח וְכָל־ עֲדָתֽוֹ׃ וּתְנ֣וּ בָהֵ֣ן׀ אֵ֡שׁ וְשִׂימוּ֩ עֲלֵיהֶ֨ן קְטֹ֜רֶת לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ מָחָ֔ר וְהָיָ֗ה הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הַקָּד֑וֹשׁ רַב־ לָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

passages.text: Moses also said to Korah, “Now listen, you sons of Levi!
passages.sermon: Moses spoke to Korah.\r\nMoses addressed the sons of Levi.\r\nMoses said, “Listen now, sons of Levi.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־ קֹ֑רַח שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֖א בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

passages.text: Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel and brought you near to Himself to perform the work at the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
passages.sermon:
The God of Israel chose you, sons of Levi.
He separated you from the rest of Israel.
He brought you close to Himself.
He gave you work at the LORD’s tabernacle.
You serve in the tabernacle.
You stand before the congregation.
You minister to the people.
passages.original: הַמְעַ֣ט מִכֶּ֗ם כִּֽי־ הִבְדִּיל֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַקְרִ֥יב אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָ֑יו לַעֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־ עֲבֹדַת֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְלַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה לְשָׁרְתָֽם׃

passages.text: He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.
passages.sermon:
God chose you, Korah.
God brought you close to Himself.
God also brought all your fellow Levites close with you.
You and your fellow Levites already serve God.
But now you want the priesthood too.
passages.original: וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ אַחֶ֥יךָ בְנֵי־ לֵוִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֖ם גַּם־ כְּהֻנָּֽה׃

passages.text: Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have conspired against the LORD! As for Aaron, who is he that you should grumble against him?”
passages.sermon:
You and all your followers have gathered together against the LORD.
You have conspired against God.
Aaron is only a man.
You have no reason to complain about Aaron.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־ עֲדָ֣תְךָ֔ הַנֹּעָדִ֖ים עַל־ יְהוָ֑ה וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן מַה־ ה֔וּא כִּ֥י תִלּוֹנוּ עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come!
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses sent a message to Dathan and Abiram.
Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab.
Moses called for Dathan and Abiram to come to him.
Dathan and Abiram refused.
They said, “We will not come.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִקְרֹ֛א לְדָתָ֥ן וְלַאֲבִירָ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיאָ֑ב וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַעֲלֶֽה׃

passages.text: Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?
passages.sermon:
Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab.
They spoke to Moses.
They said, “You brought us out of Egypt.
Egypt was a land flowing with milk and honey.
You brought us into the wilderness.
You want us to die here in the wilderness.
Is this not enough?
Now you also make yourself ruler over us.
You rule over us again and again.”
passages.original: הַמְעַ֗ט כִּ֤י הֶֽעֱלִיתָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־ תִשְׂתָּרֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ גַּם־ הִשְׂתָּרֵֽר׃

passages.text: Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? No, we will not come!”
passages.sermon:
Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab.
They spoke to Moses.
They said, “You have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey.
You have not given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards.
Will you gouge out the eyes of these men?
We will not come.”
passages.original: אַ֡ף לֹ֣א אֶל־ אֶרֶץ֩ זָבַ֨ת חָלָ֤ב וּדְבַשׁ֙ הֲבִ֣יאֹתָ֔נוּ וַתִּ֨תֶּן־ לָ֔נוּ נַחֲלַ֖ת שָׂדֶ֣ה וָכָ֑רֶם הַעֵינֵ֞י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָהֵ֛ם תְּנַקֵּ֖ר לֹ֥א נַעֲלֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses became very angry.
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses said, “Do not accept their offering.”
Moses said, “I have not taken even one donkey from them.”
Moses said, “I have not mistreated a single one of them.”
passages.original: וַיִּ֤חַר לְמֹשֶׁה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה אַל־ תֵּ֖פֶן אֶל־ מִנְחָתָ֑ם לֹ֠א חֲמ֨וֹר אֶחָ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ נָשָׂ֔אתִי וְלֹ֥א הֲרֵעֹ֖תִי אֶת־ אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow—you and they and Aaron.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Korah opposed Moses.
Moses spoke to Korah.
Moses said, “You must come before the LORD tomorrow.
All your followers must come too.
Aaron must come as well.
You, your followers, and Aaron will stand before the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־ קֹ֔רַח אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־ עֲדָ֣תְךָ֔ הֱי֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֥ה וָהֵ֛ם וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן מָחָֽר׃

passages.text: Each man is to take his censer, place incense in it, and present it before the LORD—250 censers. You and Aaron are to present your censers as well.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Korah and his followers.
Moses gave them instructions.
Each man must take his own censer.
Each man must put incense in his censer.
Each man must bring his censer before the LORD.
There are 250 censers in total.
You, Korah, must bring your censer.
Aaron must bring his censer.
Each man must bring his own censer.
passages.original: וּקְח֣וּ׀ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קְטֹ֔רֶת וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֞ם לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֔וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמָאתַ֖יִם מַחְתֹּ֑ת וְאַתָּ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן אִ֥ישׁ מַחְתָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So each man took his censer, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
Each man took his censer.
Each man put fire in his censer.
Each man put incense on the fire in his censer.
Moses stood at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Aaron stood at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
All the men stood at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֵ֔שׁ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְטֹ֑רֶת וַֽיַּעַמְד֗וּ פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וּמֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

passages.text: When Korah had gathered his whole assembly against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
passages.sermon:
Korah was a leader who opposed Moses and Aaron.
Korah gathered his entire assembly.
He brought them to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The Tent of Meeting was the place where God met with His people.
Korah and his followers stood together against Moses and Aaron.
The glory of the LORD appeared.
The glory of the LORD was visible to the whole congregation.
Everyone in the assembly saw the glory of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּקְהֵ֨ל עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם קֹ֙רַח֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיֵּרָ֥א כְבוֹד־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ כָּל־ הָעֵדָֽה׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.”
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.\r\nHe said, “Separate yourselves from this congregation.\r\nI will destroy them at once.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃ הִבָּ֣דְל֔וּ מִתּ֖וֹךְ הָעֵדָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את וַאַכַלֶּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם כְּרָֽגַע׃

passages.text: But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?”
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron were leaders of Israel.
They heard God’s warning about the people.
Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
They prayed to God.
They said, “God, You are the God of the spirits of all flesh.”
They asked God a question.
They said, “If one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?”
passages.original: וַיִּפְּל֤וּ עַל־ פְּנֵיהֶם֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֕ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָרוּחֹ֖ת לְכָל־ בָּשָׂ֑ר הָאִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ יֶחֱטָ֔א וְעַ֥ל כָּל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה תִּקְצֹֽף׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell the congregation to move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the congregation of Israel.
The LORD said, “Tell the congregation this message.”
“Move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵֽעָלוּ֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב לְמִשְׁכַּן־ קֹ֖רַח דָּתָ֥ן וַאֲבִירָֽם׃

passages.text: So Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses stood up.
Moses went to Dathan and Abiram.
The elders of Israel followed Moses.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ דָּתָ֣ן וַאֲבִירָ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ אַחֲרָ֖יו זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And he warned the congregation, “Move away now from the tents of these wicked men. Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the congregation.
He warned the people.
He said, “Move away from the tents of these wicked men.
Do not touch anything that belongs to them.
If you do, you will be swept away because of all their sins.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־ הָעֵדָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר ס֣וּרוּ נָ֡א מֵעַל֩ אָהֳלֵ֨י הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָֽרְשָׁעִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְאַֽל־ תִּגְּע֖וּ בְּכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם פֶּן־ תִּסָּפ֖וּ בְּכָל־ חַטֹּאתָֽם׃

passages.text: So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Meanwhile, Dathan and Abiram had come out and stood at the entrances to their tents with their wives and children and infants.
passages.sermon:
The people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
Dathan and Abiram came out of their tents.
They stood at the entrances to their tents.
Their wives stood with them.
Their children stood with them.
Their infants stood with them.
passages.original: וַיֵּעָל֗וּ מֵעַ֧ל מִשְׁכַּן־ קֹ֛רֶח דָּתָ֥ן וַאֲבִירָ֖ם מִסָּבִ֑יב וְדָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם יָצְא֣וּ נִצָּבִ֗ים פֶּ֚תַח אָֽהֳלֵיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם וְטַפָּֽם׃

passages.text: Then Moses said, “This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, for it was not my own doing: If these men die a natural death, or if they suffer the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people.
He said, “You will know that the LORD sent me.
The LORD sent me to do all these things.
I did not do them on my own.
If these men die as all people die, you will know something.
If these men suffer the common fate of all people, you will know something.
If this happens, the LORD did not send me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ בְּזֹאת֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן כִּֽי־ יְהוָ֣ה שְׁלָחַ֔נִי לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּי־ לֹ֖א מִלִּבִּֽי׃ אִם־ כְּמ֤וֹת כָּל־ הָֽאָדָם֙ יְמֻת֣וּן אֵ֔לֶּה וּפְקֻדַּת֙ כָּל־ הָ֣אָדָ֔ם יִפָּקֵ֖ד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃

passages.text: But if the LORD brings about something unprecedented, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD can do new and amazing things.
If the LORD creates something never seen before, you will see it.
If the earth opens its mouth, you will see it.
If the earth swallows these men, you will see it.
If the earth swallows all that belongs to them, you will see it.
If these men go down alive into Sheol, you will see it.
Then you will know this truth.
These men have shown contempt for the LORD.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּרִיאָ֞ה יִבְרָ֣א יְהוָ֗ה וּפָצְתָ֨ה הָאֲדָמָ֤ה אֶת־ פִּ֙יהָ֙ וּבָלְעָ֤ה אֹתָם֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֔ם וְיָרְד֥וּ חַיִּ֖ים שְׁאֹ֑לָה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י נִֽאֲצ֛וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: As soon as Moses had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households—all Korah’s men and all their possessions.
passages.sermon:
Moses finished speaking all these words.
The ground beneath them split open.
The earth opened its mouth.
The earth swallowed them.
The earth swallowed their households.
The earth swallowed all the men who belonged to Korah.
The earth swallowed all their possessions.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֔וֹ לְדַבֵּ֕ר אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַתִּבָּקַ֥ע הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּחְתֵּיהֶֽם׃ וַתִּפְתַּ֤ח הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶת־ פִּ֔יהָ וַתִּבְלַ֥ע אֹתָ֖ם וְאֶת־ בָּתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְקֹ֔רַח וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־ הָרֲכֽוּשׁ׃

passages.text: They went down alive into Sheol with all they owned. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from the assembly.
passages.sermon:
Korah and his followers rebelled against the LORD.
They and everything they owned went down alive into Sheol.
The earth closed over them.
They disappeared from the community.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨רְד֜וּ הֵ֣ם וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָהֶ֛ם חַיִּ֖ים שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַתְּכַ֤ס עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּאבְד֖וּ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them fled, saying, “The earth may swallow us too!”
passages.sermon:
All the Israelites stood near Korah and his followers.
The Israelites heard the cries of Korah and his followers.
The Israelites became afraid.
The Israelites ran away from that place.
The Israelites said, “The earth may swallow us too!”
passages.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר סְבִיבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נָ֣סוּ לְקֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָֽמְר֔וּ פֶּן־ תִּבְלָעֵ֖נוּ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And fire came forth from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sent out fire.
The fire came from Him.
The fire burned up 250 men.
These men were offering incense.
passages.original: וְאֵ֥שׁ יָצְאָ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וַתֹּ֗אכַל אֵ֣ת הַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּמָאתַ֙יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ מַקְרִיבֵ֖י הַקְּטֹֽרֶת׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the flames and to scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Eleazar.
Eleazar was the son of Aaron.
Aaron was the priest.
The LORD told Eleazar to remove the censers.
The censers were among the burned remains.
The LORD told Eleazar to scatter the coals far away.
The censers are holy.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ אֱמֹ֨ר אֶל־ אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־ אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְיָרֵ֤ם אֶת־ הַמַּחְתֹּת֙ מִבֵּ֣ין הַשְּׂרֵפָ֔ה וְאֶת־ הָאֵ֖שׁ זְרֵה־ הָ֑לְאָה כִּ֖י קָדֵֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: As for the censers of those who sinned at the cost of their own lives, hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for these were presented before the LORD, and so have become holy. They will serve as a sign to the Israelites.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command.
Some men sinned against God.
These men offered incense to God.
They lost their lives because of their sin.
These men used bronze censers.
God told Moses about these censers.
God said, “Take the censers from the men who sinned.”
God said, “Hammer the censers into thin sheets.”
God said, “Use these sheets to cover the altar.”
The censers became holy because they were offered before God.
The altar will now have a covering made from these censers.
This covering will be a sign to the Israelites.
The sign will remind the Israelites about what happened.
The sign will show that only those chosen by God may offer incense.
passages.original: אֵ֡ת מַחְתּוֹת֩ הַֽחַטָּאִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה בְּנַפְשֹׁתָ֗ם וְעָשׂ֨וּ אֹתָ֜ם רִקֻּעֵ֤י פַחִים֙ צִפּ֣וּי לַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי־ הִקְרִיבֻ֥ם לִפְנֵֽי־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיִּקְדָּ֑שׁוּ וְיִֽהְי֥וּ לְא֖וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers brought by those who had been burned up, and he had them hammered out to overlay the altar, just as the LORD commanded him through Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers.
passages.sermon:
Eleazar was a priest.
Eleazar was the son of Aaron.
Eleazar took the bronze censers.
The people who had been burned up had brought these censers.
Eleazar and others hammered the censers into thin sheets.
They used these sheets to cover the altar.
The LORD commanded this through Moses.
This covering was a reminder for the Israelites.
No outsider should come near to offer incense before the LORD.
An outsider is anyone who is not a descendant of Aaron.
If an outsider offers incense, he will become like Korah and his followers.
Korah and his followers died because they sinned against the LORD.
The LORD spoke this command through Moses.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֵ֚ת מַחְתּ֣וֹת הַנְּחֹ֔שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִקְרִ֖יבוּ הַשְּׂרֻפִ֑ים וַֽיְרַקְּע֖וּם צִפּ֥וּי לַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃ זִכָּר֞וֹן לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְ֠מַעַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ יִקְרַ֜ב אִ֣ישׁ זָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א מִזֶּ֤רַע אַהֲרֹן֙ ה֔וּא לְהַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֖רֶת לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֤ה כְקֹ֙רַח֙ וְכַ֣עֲדָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
The next day, all the Israelites gathered together.
They complained against Moses.
They also complained against Aaron.
They said, “You have killed the LORD’s people.”
passages.original: וַיִּלֹּ֜נוּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר אַתֶּ֥ם הֲמִתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ עַ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But when the congregation gathered against them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered together against Moses and Aaron.
Moses and Aaron were leaders chosen by God.
Moses and Aaron turned toward the Tent of Meeting.
The Tent of Meeting was the special place where God met with His people.
A cloud suddenly covered the Tent of Meeting.
The cloud showed that God’s presence was there.
The glory of the LORD appeared.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהִקָּהֵ֤ל הָֽעֵדָה֙ עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִנֵּ֥ה כִסָּ֖הוּ הֶעָנָ֑ן וַיֵּרָ֖א כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and the LORD said to Moses, “Get away from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.” And Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron were leaders of Israel.
The people of Israel gathered against them.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “Get away from this congregation.”
The LORD said, “I will consume them in an instant.”
Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן אֶל־ פְּנֵ֖י אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃פ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ הֵרֹ֗מּוּ מִתּוֹךְ֙ הָעֵדָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וַאֲכַלֶּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם כְּרָ֑גַע וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־ פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, place fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has come out from the LORD; the plague has begun.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Aaron was his brother and the high priest.
Moses spoke to Aaron.
Moses said, “Take your censer.
Put fire from the altar into the censer.
Add incense to the censer.
Go quickly to the congregation.
Make atonement for the people.
God’s wrath has come out.
A plague has begun among the people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֣ח אֶת־ הַ֠מַּחְתָּה וְתֶן־ עָלֶ֨יהָ אֵ֜שׁ מֵעַ֤ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ וְשִׂ֣ים קְטֹ֔רֶת וְהוֹלֵ֧ךְ מְהֵרָ֛ה אֶל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה וְכַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ יָצָ֥א הַקֶּ֛צֶף מִלִּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַנָּֽגֶף׃

passages.text: So Aaron took the censer as Moses had ordered and ran into the midst of the assembly. And seeing that the plague had begun among the people, he offered the incense and made atonement for the people.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the high priest of Israel.
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses gave Aaron a command.
Aaron took his censer, as Moses had ordered.
Aaron ran into the midst of the assembly.
Aaron saw that the plague had begun among the people.
Aaron put incense in the censer.
Aaron made atonement for the people.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ דִּבֶּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיָּ֙רָץ֙ אֶל־ תּ֣וֹך הַקָּהָ֔ל וְהִנֵּ֛ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַנֶּ֖גֶף בָּעָ֑ם וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶֽת־ הַקְּטֹ֔רֶת וַיְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was a priest of Israel.
\r\nAaron stood between the living people and the dead people.
\r\nThe plague stopped.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד בֵּֽין־ הַמֵּתִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַֽחַיִּ֑ים וַתֵּעָצַ֖ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃

passages.text: But those who died from the plague numbered 14,700, in addition to those who had died on account of Korah.
passages.sermon:
The plague killed many people among the Israelites.
The number of people who died from the plague was 14,700.
This number does not include those who died because of Korah’s rebellion.
Korah’s rebellion had already caused other deaths before the plague.
passages.original: וַיִּהְי֗וּ הַמֵּתִים֙ בַּמַּגֵּפָ֔ה אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר אֶ֖לֶף וּשְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֑וֹת מִלְּבַ֥ד הַמֵּתִ֖ים עַל־ דְּבַר־ קֹֽרַח׃

passages.text: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, since the plague had been halted.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the high priest of Israel.
Moses was the leader of Israel.
A plague had struck the people of Israel.
Aaron returned to Moses.
He went to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The Tent of Meeting was the place where God met with Moses and Aaron.
The plague had stopped.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה נֶעֱצָֽרָה׃פ
